# Bonsai: full reference for LLMs

Bonsai (`bonsai-js` on npm) is a small, total, typed expression language for JavaScript. It evaluates untrusted expression text against host data without executing JavaScript. Every expression terminates: there are no loops, recursion, or assignment. An expression reaches host code only through functions the host declared and data the host put in the context.

Entry points: `bonsai-js` (environment, types, errors) and `bonsai-js/service` (editor features). ESM only, zero dependencies. Runtimes: Node.js 22+, current Bun, modern ESM browsers.

## Quick start

```ts
import { bonsai, fn, t } from 'bonsai-js'

const env = bonsai({
  variables: {
    customer: t.object({ tier: t.enum('standard', 'gold'), email: t.optional(t.string()) }),
    cart: t.object({ items: t.list(t.object({ price: t.number(), qty: t.number() })) }),
  },
})

env.check('customer.teir == "gold"').ok // false: UNKNOWN_PROPERTY, did you mean "tier"?
const freeShipping = env.compile('customer.tier == "gold" || cart.items.map(.price * .qty).sum() >= 50', {
  expect: t.boolean(),
})
freeShipping.evaluateSync({ customer: { tier: 'standard' }, cart: { items: [{ price: 20, qty: 3 }] } }) // true
env.evaluateSync('customer.email ?? "no email"', ctx) // one-off evaluation, compiled once and cached
```

## Values

- `null`: the single absent value. Missing properties, missing variables, and host `undefined` read as `null`.
- boolean, number (IEEE-754 double; NaN/Infinity results are errors), string (UTF-16; `length` counts code units).
- list (host arrays, read by index, never mutated), map (plain objects and class instances via own enumerable properties; object literals). A value may have more keys than its declared type lists. Keys follow JavaScript property order: integer-like keys first, ascending, then insertion order.
- timestamp (a host `Date`, `now()`, `timestamp("2026-01-01T00:00:00Z")`), duration (`days(3)`, `t1 - t2`).
- Opaque: functions, symbols, bigints, and built-in host objects (`Map`, `Set`, `WeakMap`, `WeakSet`, `RegExp`, promises and thenables, `ArrayBuffer` and typed arrays, errors, boxed primitives). Comparable with `==` and passable to host functions; reading a property is a `TYPE_ERROR`.
- `type(x)` returns "null", "boolean", "number", "string", "list", "map", "timestamp", "duration", or "opaque".

## Syntax

- Literals: `42`, `3.14`, `1e-3`, `1_000`, `0xff`, `0xde_ad`, `0b101`, `0o17` (a number starts with a digit: `.5` is invalid), `"text"`, `'text'`, `true`, `false`, `null`, `[1, ...rest]`, `{ a: 1, "b-c": 2, [key]: 3, ...other, name }`.
- Comments: `// line` and `/* block */`.
- Templates: `` `Hello ${name}` ``. `null` renders as empty text, timestamps and durations as ISO-8601, lists and maps are a type error.
- Reserved: `true false null let in not`. `has(...)` and `try(...)` are special forms. `|>` is reserved and is a syntax error.

## Operators (loosest to tightest)

1. `let x = e; body`
2. `c ? a : b` (right-associative)
3. `??`
4. `||`
5. `&&`
6. `==` `!=` (do not chain)
7. `<` `<=` `>` `>=` `in` `not in` (do not chain)
8. `+` `-`
9. `*` `/` `%`
10. `**` (right-associative)
11. prefix `!` `-`
12. `.` `?.` `[]` `?.[]` calls

Syntax errors instead of silent groupings: `??` mixed with `&&`/`||` without parentheses, `-x ** 2`, `a < b < c`, `a == b == c`.

- Equality: by value, no coercion. `1 == "1"` false; `[1, [2]] == [1, [2]]` true; maps compare by keys and values in any order; timestamps by instant; different kinds are unequal (never an error). `x == null` is true for missing or null.
- Ordering: two numbers, two strings, two timestamps, or two durations. If either side is `null` the result is `false` (so `users.filter(.age >= 18)` skips users without an age). Other mixes are type errors.
- Arithmetic: `+` on numbers, strings, lists, durations; timestamp +/- duration; timestamp - timestamp = duration; duration * or / number; duration / duration = number. No other combination: `null + 1`, `"a" + 1`, `t + 30` are errors. Division by zero is an error.
- Logic: `!`, `&&`, `||`, `?:` accept booleans and `null` (false); anything else is a type error. `&&`/`||` short-circuit and return booleans. `a ?? b` evaluates `b` only when `a` is `null`.
- Membership: `x in list` (by `==`), `"sub" in "string"`, `"key" in map`, `x in null` is false, `x not in y`.

## Property access

- `a.b` reads an own property of a map; missing is `null`; any property of `null` is `null`. Strings and lists have only `length`; other reads on non-maps are type errors.
- `a[k]`: string keys on maps (numbers become decimal text), integer indices on lists and strings (out of range, negative, or fractional is `null`; use `at(-1)`), `null` receiver or key gives `null`.
- `?.` equals `.` for reads. For calls it makes that one call return `null` when the receiver is `null`; it does not skip the rest of the chain: write `a?.trim()?.toUpperCase()`.
- Calling a function with `null` as the first argument, when no overload accepts null, is a `NULL_RECEIVER` error.
- `__proto__`, `constructor`, `prototype` are never readable or valid keys.
- `has(a.b)` / `has(a[k])`: whether the own key (or list index) exists, even if the value is `null`.

## Functions and lambdas

- One namespace: `f(x, a)` and `x.f(a)` are the same call. `f` always resolves to a built-in or declared host function, never to a value in data.
- Built-ins are overloaded on parameter types; the overload is chosen statically when types are known, otherwise by runtime kinds.
- A host function with a built-in's name replaces it in that environment.
- Lambdas are arguments for function parameters only: `users.filter(u => u.age >= 18)`, `orders.map((o, i) => ...)`.
- Implicit `.`: `users.filter(.age >= 18 && !.suspended)`, `xs.map(. * 2)`, `rows.map(.[0])`. `.` binds to the nearest enclosing argument whose parameter is a function, skipping ordinary parameters: `users.filter(.score > max(.bonus, 10))` compares each user's own fields; `groups.map(.users.filter(.active).length)`.
- `.` directly inside an explicit lambda body is an error; name the outer item: `orders.filter(o => o.lines.some(.sku == o.promoSku))`.
- Higher-order functions call lambdas in order and stop early when the result is known.

## let, try, has

- `let total = items.map(.price * .qty).sum(); total > 100 ? total * 0.9 : total`. Bindings may shadow context variables, not other bindings.
- `try(expr, fallback)` catches evaluation errors (type errors, invalid arguments, division by zero, host functions that throw), never syntax, check, or limit errors, and never `HOST_CONTRACT`.

## Time

Timestamps are instants; durations are exact (a day is 24 hours). Calendar functions take an optional IANA time zone and default to UTC: `year(t, tz)`, `startOfDay(t, tz)`, `addMonths(t, 1, tz)`, `formatDate(t, pattern, tz)`. `now()` is read once per evaluation from the environment clock. `addDays` keeps wall-clock time across DST; `+ days(n)` keeps exact length.

## Static checking

Gradual: unknown values are `any` (open environments, undeclared variables in non-strict environments, open records, and `values()`/`entries()`/computed reads on declared objects, which may carry extra keys). Declaring `variables` makes an environment strict unless `strict: false`. Errors: `UNKNOWN_VARIABLE` (strict), `UNKNOWN_PROPERTY` (closed records and map literals), `UNKNOWN_FUNCTION`, `NO_OVERLOAD`, `TYPE_ERROR`, `NULLABLE_RECEIVER`, `INVALID_LAMBDA`, `BLOCKED_PROPERTY`, `EXPECTED_TYPE`, `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, plus `SYNTAX` and `LIMIT` from `check()`. Warnings (severity "warning"): `ALWAYS_FALSE` (comparisons that can never hold), `MAYBE_NULL` (ordering comparisons with possibly-null values, lambdas that may return null where a boolean is expected), `NEVER_NULL` (`??` on never-null values).

## API

### bonsai(options) -> Environment

Options: `variables` (Record of types), `strict` (undeclared variables are errors; default true when `variables` is given), `functions` (host functions), `libraries` (`{ name, functions?, variables? }[]`, duplicate names are errors), `limits`, `cacheSize` (compiled programs cached, default 256), `clock` (`() => Date`), `validateContext` (check the context against declared types before each evaluation; fails with `INVALID_CONTEXT`).

Environment members:
- `check(src, { expect? })` -> `{ ok, type, diagnostics }`; never throws.
- `compile(src, { expect? })` -> Program; throws `BonsaiSyntaxError`, `BonsaiCheckError`, `BonsaiLimitError`.
- `evaluateSync(src, ctx?, options?)`, `evaluate(src, ctx?, options?)`: compile through an LRU cache (`cacheSize`, default 256) and evaluate.
- `extend(options)` -> new environment with more variables/functions/libraries.
- `listFunctions()`, `describeFunction(name)` -> `{ name, description, host, async, signatures: [{ params, required, rest?, returns }] }`.
- `parse(src)` -> syntax tree; `variables`; `strict`.

Evaluation options: `timeout` (ms), `maxSteps`, `signal` (AbortSignal).

### Program

`source`, `ast`, `type`, `async`, `warnings`, `references: { variables, functions }`, `evaluate(ctx?, options?)`, `evaluateSync(ctx?, options?)`. Results are plain values; timestamps are `Date`; durations are `Duration` (`ms`, ISO `toString()`).

### Host functions

```ts
fn({
  params: [t.string(), t.optional(t.number())],
  required: 1, // later parameters are optional, must be nullable, and arrive as null when omitted
  rest: t.number(), // optional variadic type
  returns: t.boolean(),
  async: false, // true: run returns a promise; evaluateSync rejects the expression with ASYNC_IN_SYNC; a promise from a non-async function is HOST_CONTRACT
  context: false, // true: run(ctx, ...args)
  description: 'Shown in listFunctions and editor hovers',
  cost: 32, // steps charged per call (default 32); lower for cheap pure helpers
  run: (name, count) => true,
})
```

Arguments are validated before `run`; results are checked deeply against `returns` (`HOST_CONTRACT` otherwise, not caught by `try`); exceptions (even a `BonsaiError`) become `HOST_ERROR` with `cause`. `withContext<Ctx>()` returns an `fn` variant whose `run` receives a typed context.

### Types (t)

`t.string()`, `t.number()`, `t.boolean()`, `t.null()`, `t.timestamp()`, `t.duration()`, `t.literal(v)`, `t.enum(...values)`, `t.list(T)`, `t.object({ ... })` (closed), `t.record(V)` (open; reads are `V | null`), `t.optional(T)` (`T | null`, also optional key), `t.union(...)`, `t.opaque(name)`, `t.any()`, `t.never()`. `Infer<typeof T>` gives the TypeScript type. `formatType(type)`, `isAssignable(source, target)`. Types are JSON-serializable.

### Errors

All errors from checking and evaluating extend `BonsaiError` with `code`, `source`, `span` (`{ start, end }`), `position` (1-based), `formatted` (message + code frame); exceptions from host code (functions, getters, Proxies, including a `BonsaiError` a host function throws) are wrapped as `HOST_ERROR`. Invalid configuration throws `TypeError` or `RangeError` from `bonsai()`, `fn()`, `evaluate*()` (per-evaluation options), and `print()` (trees the parser could not produce).
- `BonsaiSyntaxError`: `SYNTAX`
- `BonsaiCheckError`: `CHECK` (`.diagnostics`)
- `BonsaiLimitError`: `SOURCE_TOO_LONG`, `TOO_DEEP`, `TOO_MANY_NODES`, `TOO_COMPLEX`, `STEP_LIMIT`, `STRING_LIMIT`, `LIST_LIMIT`, `PATTERN_LIMIT`, `TIMEOUT`, `ABORTED`
- `BonsaiRuntimeError`: `TYPE_ERROR`, `NO_OVERLOAD`, `NULL_RECEIVER`, `DIVISION_BY_ZERO`, `NON_FINITE`, `BLOCKED_PROPERTY`, `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `ASYNC_IN_SYNC`, `HOST_ERROR`, `HOST_CONTRACT`, `INVALID_CONTEXT`

### Limits (defaults)

`maxSourceLength` 100000, `maxDepth` 128, `maxNodes` 20000, `maxSteps` 1000000 (0 disables; charged by the real cost of each operation, deterministic), `maxStringLength` 100000, `maxListLength` 100000, `maxValueDepth` 64 (values built or walked), `maxPatternLength` 4096 (regex patterns, `PATTERN_LIMIT`), `timeout` 0 (none). Each host call costs its function's `cost` (default 32 steps).

### Language service (bonsai-js/service)

`createLanguageService(env)` -> `{ complete(src, offset), hover(src, offset), diagnostics(src) }`. `complete` returns `{ start, end, items: [{ label, kind, detail, documentation?, insertText, range? }] }` with kinds `value`, `variable`, `local`, `property`, `function`, `method`, `keyword`. It never evaluates or calls host functions.

## Security model

Expression text is untrusted; context data and host functions are trusted. Expressions cannot run code, reach prototypes or globals, call functions found in data, trigger conversion hooks, mutate data, or run unbounded: the step budget charges every operation for its real cost, including text search, regular expressions, sorting, and time zone math. Built-ins never run host code on receivers (no iterators, species, or methods). Host functions run with full privileges and cannot be interrupted while running synchronously; getters and Proxies in the context run when read. Declared types are not access control: `keys()`, `values()`, `entries()`, and dynamic indexing read every own enumerable property of the data passed in.

## Migrating from 0.x

`a |> f(b)` -> `a.f(b)`; `upper`/`lower` -> `toUpperCase`/`toLowerCase`; `flatten` -> `flat`; stdlib plugins -> built in; `addFunction` -> `functions: { name: fn({...}) }`; `addContextFunction` -> `fn({ context: true, ... })`; `validate()` -> `check()`; `evaluateExpression` -> `bonsai().evaluateSync`; `allowedProperties` -> pass only the data expressions may read; `x == null` now includes missing values; `&&`/`||` are strict booleans (use `??` for defaults). Results that changed silently: `round` rounds halves away from zero and honors digits; `avg([])` is null; `unique` compares by value; templates render null as empty text and dates as ISO-8601; `toNumber` of invalid text is an error; division and remainder by zero are errors; `sort()` is numeric; `includes`/`indexOf`/`in` and `Date` equality compare by value; `replace` inserts its replacement literally; `substring` -> `slice` and `charAt` -> `at` differ for reversed or negative positions. Requires Node.js 22+. Full guide: https://danfry1.github.io/bonsai-js/guide/migrating

## Built-in functions

Every built-in is callable as `f(x, ...)` or `x.f(...)`. `?` marks an optional parameter.

### Text

- toUpperCase(string): string: Upper-cases text.
- toLowerCase(string): string: Lower-cases text.
- trim(string): string: Removes leading and trailing whitespace.
- trimStart(string): string: Removes leading whitespace.
- trimEnd(string): string: Removes trailing whitespace.
- startsWith(string, string): boolean: Whether text starts with a prefix.
- endsWith(string, string): boolean: Whether text ends with a suffix.
- includes(string, string): boolean: Whether text contains a substring, or a list contains a value.
- indexOf(string, string): number: Position of the first match, or -1.
- lastIndexOf(string, string): number: Position of the last match, or -1.
- slice(string, number, number?): string: A section of text or a list; negative positions count from the end.
- split(string, string, number?): string[]: Splits text on a separator.
- replace(string, string, string): string: Replaces the first occurrence of some text (no patterns).
- replaceAll(string, string, string): string: Replaces every occurrence of some text (no patterns).
- padStart(string, number, string?): string: Pads text at the start to a length.
- padEnd(string, number, string?): string: Pads text at the end to a length.
- repeat(string, number): string: Repeats text a number of times.
- at(string, number): string | null: The item or character at a position; negative positions count from the end.
- matches(string, string): boolean: Whether text contains a match for a regular expression (JavaScript syntax as with the u flag, without backreferences or lookaround; linear time; anchor with ^ and $; prefix (?i) to ignore case).
- toString(string | number | boolean | null | timestamp | duration): string: Renders a value as text, as a template would.
- toNumber(string | number): number: Parses text as a number.

### Lists

- map(T[], (T, number) => U): U[]: Transforms each item.
- filter(T[], (T, number) => boolean): T[]: Keeps the items for which the lambda is true.
- find(T[], (T, number) => boolean): T | null: The first item for which the lambda is true, or null.
- findIndex(T[], (T, number) => boolean): number: The position of the first item for which the lambda is true, or -1.
- some(T[], (T, number) => boolean): boolean: Whether the lambda is true for at least one item.
- every(T[], (T, number) => boolean): boolean: Whether the lambda is true for every item.
- none(T[], (T, number) => boolean): boolean: Whether the lambda is false for every item.
- count(T[]): number; count(T[], (T, number) => boolean): number: The number of items, or of items for which the lambda is true.
- flatMap(T[], (T, number) => U[] | U): U[]: Transforms each item and flattens list results one level.
- reduce(T[], (U, T) => U, U): U: Folds a list into one value: reduce(list, (acc, item) => ..., initial).
- sort(T[], ("asc" | "desc")?): T[]: Sorts numbers, text, timestamps, or durations; pass "desc" to reverse.
- sortBy(T[], (T, number) => K, ("asc" | "desc")?): T[]: Sorts by a key; pass "desc" to reverse. Nulls sort first.
- groupBy(T[], (T, number) => string | number | boolean): { [key: string]: T[] }: Groups items into a map of lists by a key.
- reverse(T[]): T[]: The items in reverse order.
- unique(T[]): T[]: The items without duplicates (by value), in first-seen order.
- flat(any[]): any[]: Flattens nested lists one level.
- first(T[]): T | null: The first item, or null.
- last(T[]): T | null: The last item, or null.
- join((string | number | boolean | null | timestamp | duration)[], string?): string: Joins items into text with a separator (default ",").
- slice(T[], number, number?): T[]: A section of text or a list; negative positions count from the end.
- at(T[], number): T | null: The item or character at a position; negative positions count from the end.
- includes(T[], any): boolean: Whether text contains a substring, or a list contains a value.
- indexOf(T[], any): number: Position of the first match, or -1.
- lastIndexOf(T[], any): number: Position of the last match, or -1.
- isEmpty(any[] | string | { [key: string]: any } | null): boolean: Whether a list, text, or map has no items; null is empty.
- min(T[]): T | null: The smallest value (nulls are skipped); null for an empty list.
- max(T[]): T | null: The largest value (nulls are skipped); null for an empty list.
- sum((number | null)[]): number; sum((duration | null)[]): duration: The sum of the numbers in a list (nulls are skipped).
- avg((number | null)[]): number | null: The mean of the numbers in a list (nulls are skipped); null for no numbers.

### Numbers

- round(number, number?): number: Rounds half away from zero, optionally to a number of decimal digits.
- floor(number): number: Rounds down.
- ceil(number): number: Rounds up.
- trunc(number): number: Drops the fractional part.
- abs(number): number: Absolute value.
- sqrt(number): number: Square root.
- clamp(number, number, number): number: Limits a number to a range.
- toFixed(number, number): string: Formats a number with a fixed number of decimals.
- formatNumber(number, number?, string?): string: Formats a number with grouping, e.g. 1,234.5, with optional decimals and locale (default "en-US").
- formatCurrency(number, string, string?): string: Formats an amount in a currency (ISO 4217 code such as "EUR"), with an optional locale (default "en-US").
- min(T[]): T | null; min(number, ...number): number: The smallest value (nulls are skipped); null for an empty list.
- max(T[]): T | null; max(number, ...number): number: The largest value (nulls are skipped); null for an empty list.
- sum((number | null)[]): number: The sum of the numbers in a list (nulls are skipped).
- avg((number | null)[]): number | null: The mean of the numbers in a list (nulls are skipped); null for no numbers.

### Maps and Values

- keys({ [key: string]: any }): string[]: The keys of a map.
- values({ [key: string]: T }): T[]: The values of a map.
- entries({ [key: string]: T }): { key: string, value: T }[]: The { key, value } pairs of a map.
- isEmpty(any[] | string | { [key: string]: any } | null): boolean: Whether a list, text, or map has no items; null is empty.
- type(any): string: The kind of a value: "null", "boolean", "number", "string", "list", "map", "timestamp", "duration", or "opaque".
- toString(string | number | boolean | null | timestamp | duration): string: Renders a value as text, as a template would.

### Time

- now(): timestamp: The current time, fixed for one evaluation.
- timestamp(string): timestamp; timestamp(number): timestamp; timestamp(timestamp): timestamp: Parses ISO-8601 text or epoch milliseconds into a timestamp.
- weeks(number): duration: A duration of n weeks.
- days(number): duration: A duration of n days (24 hours each).
- hours(number): duration: A duration of n hours.
- minutes(number): duration: A duration of n minutes.
- seconds(number): duration: A duration of n seconds.
- milliseconds(number): duration: A duration of n milliseconds.
- inDays(duration): number: A duration as a (fractional) number of days.
- inHours(duration): number: A duration as a number of hours.
- inMinutes(duration): number: A duration as a number of minutes.
- inSeconds(duration): number: A duration as a number of seconds.
- inMilliseconds(duration): number: A duration as a number of milliseconds.
- year(timestamp, string?): number: The calendar year, in a time zone (default UTC).
- month(timestamp, string?): number: The month 1-12, in a time zone (default UTC).
- day(timestamp, string?): number: The day of the month, in a time zone (default UTC).
- hour(timestamp, string?): number: The hour 0-23, in a time zone (default UTC).
- minute(timestamp, string?): number: The minute, in a time zone (default UTC).
- second(timestamp, string?): number: The second, in a time zone (default UTC).
- dayOfWeek(timestamp, string?): number: The ISO weekday (Monday 1 to Sunday 7), in a time zone (default UTC).
- startOfDay(timestamp, string?): timestamp: Midnight at the start of the day, in a time zone (default UTC).
- startOfMonth(timestamp, string?): timestamp: Midnight on the first of the month, in a time zone (default UTC).
- startOfYear(timestamp, string?): timestamp: Midnight on January 1, in a time zone (default UTC).
- addDays(timestamp, number, string?): timestamp: Adds calendar days (keeps the wall-clock time across DST), in a time zone.
- addMonths(timestamp, number, string?): timestamp: Adds calendar months, clamping the day to the month length.
- addYears(timestamp, number, string?): timestamp: Adds calendar years (Feb 29 becomes Feb 28).
- formatDate(timestamp, string, string?): string: Formats a timestamp in a time zone (default UTC). Tokens: yyyy yy MMMM MMM MM M dd d EEEE EEE HH H hh h a mm m ss s SSS; quote literal text.
- abs(duration): duration: Absolute value.
- sum((duration | null)[]): duration: The sum of the numbers in a list (nulls are skipped).
